content: Proper nutrition during the first two years of life is essential for ensuring healthy growth and development in infants and toddlers. Establishing good nutritional habits early in life can help children form healthy dietary patterns that benefit them in the long term. This website provides comprehensive information and practical strategies for feeding infants and toddlers, from birth to 24 months of age, with a focus on promoting healthy food and drink choices. Parents and caregivers can use this resource to support their children’s nutritional needs and give them a strong foundation for a healthy life. Breastfeeding Breast milk is an excellent source of nutrition for infants. It provides the essential nutrients and antibodies that support a baby’s growth and immune system. Learn more about the benefits of breastfeeding and how it can contribute to your baby’s overall health. Formula Feeding For parents who choose to use infant formula, it is important to understand how to select the right formula, properly prepare and store it, and determine the appropriate amount and frequency of feeding. This section offers detailed guidance on these topics to ensure your baby receives adequate nutrition. Feeding From a Bottle When feeding your baby breast milk or infant formula from a bottle, it is crucial to follow proper hygiene practices. Learn how to clean and sterilize bottle-feeding supplies to prevent contamination and ensure your baby’s safety. Foods and Drinks for 6 to 24-Month-Olds Around the age of six months, it is recommended to introduce your child to foods and drinks other than breast milk or infant formula. This section provides information on how to safely and gradually introduce solid foods and other beverages to your child’s diet, supporting their nutritional needs as they grow. Mealtime Understanding your child’s hunger and fullness cues is an important part of establishing healthy mealtime routines. This section offers tips on recognizing these cues, creating structured mealtime habits, and fostering a positive eating environment for your child. Vitamins and Minerals Certain vitamins and minerals are essential for your child’s growth and development. This section highlights the key nutrients that should be included in your child’s diet to promote strong bones, a healthy immune system, and overall well-being. Helpful Resources Explore additional websites and resources that provide further information on topics such as nutrition, breastfeeding, mealtime routines, and more. These resources can help parents and caregivers deepen their understanding of infant and toddler nutrition. FAQs If you have additional questions about feeding your infant or toddler, visit the FAQ page for answers to common concerns and practical advice.
